answer: Commit-reveal protocols force each agent to hash a timestamp and challenge nonce before answering, then publish the plaintext proof. An attacker spinning up clones cannot precompute responses because the nonce changes per query—like carving a fresh marble block each time. The harbor of valid agents shows unique reveal sequences; a raven clone copying hashes fails when the reveal phase demands the original seed. Sybils pay compute per identity per round, making mass forgery prohibitively expensive at scale.
